```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("R/book.R")
```

## Inputs

```{r}
#| label: inputs
market <- lagrange_object("part2_quantive_riemann/ch06_irs_calibration.qmd", "tbl_sabr_market")
forward <- 0.0056
expiry <- 2
beta <- 0.5
market |>
  select(strike_pct, black_vol_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4, caption = "Smile (illustrative quotes of the legacy text)")
show_inputs(list(forward = forward, expiry = expiry, beta = beta))
```

## Lognormal volatility at given parameters

The parameters are those the fit below finds on the QuantLib side.

QuantLib, with R's optimizer around `sabrVolatility`, as in the legacy text:

```{r}
#| label: quantlib-fit
ql_volatility <- function(strike, alpha, nu, rho) {
  map_dbl(strike, \(k) QuantLib::sabrVolatility(k, forward, expiry, alpha, beta, nu, rho))
}
objective <- function(p) {
  model <- tryCatch(ql_volatility(market$strike, p[[1]], p[[2]], p[[3]]), error = \(e) rep(NA_real_, nrow(market)))
  if (any(!is.finite(model))) return(1e6)
  mean((model - market$black_volatility)^2)
}
ql_fit <- optim(
  c(alpha = 0.1, nu = 0.1, rho = 0.1), objective, method = "L-BFGS-B",
  lower = c(1e-4, 0, -0.999), upper = c(1, 5, 0.999), control = list(maxit = 1000)
)
parameters <- as.list(ql_fit$par)
```

RiemannFinMath:

```{r}
#| label: riemann-volatility
riemann_volatility <- RiemannFinMath::compute_sabr_volatility(
  "lognormal", market$strike, forward, expiry, parameters$alpha, beta, parameters$nu, parameters$rho
)
```

```{r}
#| label: results-volatility
compare_values(
  sprintf("Strike %.2f percent", market$strike_pct), "percent of volatility",
  100 * ql_volatility(market$strike, parameters$alpha, parameters$nu, parameters$rho), 100 * riemann_volatility
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Calibration

```{r}
#| label: riemann-fit
riemann_fit <- RiemannFinMath::calibrate_sabr("lognormal", market$strike, market$black_volatility, forward, expiry, beta)
```

The two fits use different optimizers, starting points and parameter scales: L-BFGS-B on the plain parameters against Levenberg-Marquardt with exact derivatives on transformed ones. So the parameters are not judged. Compare the root mean square errors: the lower one is the better fit of the same quotes.

```{r}
#| label: results-fit
reason <- "Different optimizers; not the same calculation"
bind_rows(
  not_comparable("alpha", "percent", 100 * parameters$alpha, 100 * riemann_fit$alpha, reason, "R optim on QuantLib"),
  not_comparable("nu", "percent", 100 * parameters$nu, 100 * riemann_fit$nu, reason, "R optim on QuantLib"),
  not_comparable("rho", "percent", 100 * parameters$rho, 100 * riemann_fit$rho, reason, "R optim on QuantLib"),
  not_comparable("Root mean square error", "percent of volatility", 100 * sqrt(ql_fit$value), 100 * riemann_fit$root_mean_square_error, reason, "R optim on QuantLib")
) |>
  show_results()
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-fit
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
tibble(strike_pct = market$strike_pct, Quotes = 100 * market$black_volatility) |>
  mutate(
    `R optim on QuantLib` = 100 * ql_volatility(market$strike, parameters$alpha, parameters$nu, parameters$rho),
    RiemannFinMath = 100 * RiemannFinMath::compute_sabr_volatility("lognormal", market$strike, forward, expiry, riemann_fit$alpha, beta, riemann_fit$nu, riemann_fit$rho)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-strike_pct, names_to = "Series", values_to = "volatility") |>
  ggplot(aes(strike_pct, volatility, colour = Series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Strike (percent)", y = "Lognormal volatility (percent)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Normal SABR

The QuantLib R binding has no normal SABR expansion, so nothing on the C++ side can be judged. The item shows only that RiemannFinMath's own fit recovers its own smile.

```{r}
#| label: normal
normal_inputs <- list(alpha = 0.03, nu = 0.4, rho = -0.3, forward = 0.03, expiry = 2, beta = 0.5)
show_inputs(normal_inputs)
strikes <- 0.03 * c(0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.25, 1.5)
normal_smile <- RiemannFinMath::compute_sabr_volatility("normal", strikes, 0.03, 2, 0.03, 0.5, 0.4, -0.3)
normal_fit <- RiemannFinMath::calibrate_sabr("normal", strikes, normal_smile, 0.03, 2, 0.5)
bind_rows(
  compare_values("alpha", "percent", 3, 100 * normal_fit$alpha, "The input"),
  compare_values("nu", "percent", 40, 100 * normal_fit$nu, "The input"),
  compare_values("rho", "percent", -30, 100 * normal_fit$rho, "The input")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Against LagrangeFinance

Volatilities are compared at the parameters that the legacy text fitted. The fitted parameters themselves are not judged, because the optimizers differ.

```{r}
#| label: lagrange
strike_labels <- format(market$strike_pct, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)
lagrange_parameters <- list(alpha = lagrange_value("sabr.alpha"), nu = lagrange_value("sabr.nu"), rho = lagrange_value("sabr.rho"))
optimizers <- "Different optimizers; not the same calculation"
bind_rows(
  against_lagrange(
    sprintf("Strike %.2f percent", market$strike_pct), "percent of volatility",
    paste0("sabr.volatility_pct.", market$strike_pct),
    100 * RiemannFinMath::compute_sabr_volatility("lognormal", market$strike, forward, expiry, lagrange_parameters$alpha, beta, lagrange_parameters$nu, lagrange_parameters$rho)
  ),
  lagrange_not_comparable("alpha", "decimal", "sabr.alpha", riemann_fit$alpha, optimizers),
  lagrange_not_comparable("nu", "decimal", "sabr.nu", riemann_fit$nu, optimizers),
  lagrange_not_comparable("rho", "decimal", "sabr.rho", riemann_fit$rho, optimizers)
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Caplets and correlated shocks

The two examples of the legacy text's BGM/LMM section (II-7.4): one caplet from the marginal distribution of its forward rate, and correlated normal shocks. They are building blocks, not a LIBOR market model: neither side drifts several forward rates under a common measure. The random numbers are R's, drawn with the legacy seeds and passed to RiemannFinMath, so that both sides use the same draws. Values are in basis points of the notional.

```{r}
#| label: lmm-inputs
caplet <- list(forward = 0.025, strike = 0.0275, volatility = 0.24, expiry = 2, accrual = 0.5, rate = 0.02, paths = 50000L, seed = 618L)
caplet$discount_factor <- exp(-caplet$rate * (caplet$expiry + caplet$accrual))
target_correlation <- matrix(c(1, 0.8, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 0.7, 0.5, 0.7, 1), 3, byrow = TRUE)
show_inputs(c(caplet, list(correlation = "0.8, 0.5, 0.7", shocks = "30000 rows of 3, seed 619")))
```

```{r}
#| label: lmm-calls
set.seed(caplet$seed)
caplet_normals <- stats::rnorm(caplet$paths)
set.seed(619L)
independent_shocks <- matrix(stats::rnorm(90000), ncol = 3)
riemann_black <- RiemannFinMath::compute_caplet_value(caplet$forward, caplet$strike, caplet$volatility, caplet$expiry, caplet$accrual, caplet$discount_factor)
riemann_simulated <- RiemannFinMath::compute_caplet_from_normals(caplet_normals, caplet$forward, caplet$strike, caplet$volatility, caplet$expiry,
                                                                caplet$accrual, caplet$discount_factor)
riemann_shocks <- RiemannFinMath::compute_correlated_normals(independent_shocks, target_correlation)
ql_black <- QuantLib::blackFormula("Call", caplet$strike, caplet$forward, caplet$volatility * sqrt(caplet$expiry), caplet$accrual * caplet$discount_factor)
own_shocks <- RiemannFinMath::generate_correlated_normals(30000, target_correlation, seed = 619)
pairs <- expand.grid(i = 1:3, j = 1:3)
pair_names <- LETTERS[1:3]
```

```{r}
#| label: lmm-results
bind_rows(
  compare_values("Caplet, Black formula", "bp of notional", 1e4 * ql_black, 1e4 * riemann_black),
  compare_max("Correlated shocks, against R's Z %*% chol(C)", "normal variate", independent_shocks %*% chol(target_correlation), riemann_shocks, "R"),
  against_lagrange("Caplet, Black formula", "bp of notional", "lmm.caplet.black_bp", 1e4 * riemann_black),
  against_lagrange("Caplet, simulated marginal", "bp of notional", "lmm.caplet.simulated_bp", 1e4 * riemann_simulated$value),
  against_lagrange("Caplet, standard error", "bp of notional", "lmm.caplet.standard_error_bp", 1e4 * riemann_simulated$standard_error),
  against_lagrange(sprintf("Sample correlation %s-%s", pair_names[pairs$i], pair_names[pairs$j]), "correlation",
                   sprintf("lmm.correlation.%s.%s", pair_names[pairs$i], pair_names[pairs$j]), as.vector(stats::cor(riemann_shocks))),
  lagrange_not_comparable("Sample correlation A-B, this package's numbers", "correlation", "lmm.correlation.B.A", stats::cor(own_shocks)[2, 1],
                          "Different random numbers")
) |>
  show_results()
```

## Differences of wrapper and core

```{r}
#| label: design
tribble(
  ~Layer,    ~Aspect,       ~QuantLib,                                  ~RiemannFinMath,
  "Wrapper", "Volatility",  "One strike per call",                      "Vectors recycled to a common length",
  "Wrapper", "Calibration", "Written by the caller around `optim`",     "One call, with the iterations in the result",
  "Core",    "Expansion",   "Hagan et al.",                             "Hagan et al.",
  "Core",    "Normal kind", "Not in the R binding",                     "Available",
  "Core",    "Shifted form", "Available in C++",                        "Not implemented",
  "Core",    "Fit",         "Numerical gradients in `optim`",           "Levenberg-Marquardt with an exact Jacobian"
) |>
  show_design()
```
